# Unknown device workflow URI compatibility (2026-05-24 18:53Z)

_**User**_

Requested a deep analysis and implementation plan for the workflow around adding new or unknown devices:

- Tapping an unknown device row should show the same actions as tapping the options button.
- Opening Miataru from an unknown-device notification should show an explanatory decision dialog.
- Opening a `miataru://<DeviceID>` URI from the Camera app should open known devices directly and open the add-device dialog for unknown devices.
- Existing URI scheme handling must remain compatible.

---

_**Agent**_

Implemented the unknown-device workflow:

- Added centralized device-link parsing and generation through `DeviceLinkResolver`.
- Routed canonical `miataru://<DeviceID>` links through `AppNavigationCoordinator`.
- Preserved QR generation, QR scanner input, and external URI compatibility.
- Added app-wide navigation requests for opening the Devices tab, opening known devices, presenting add-device sheets, and presenting unknown-device actions.
- Wired unknown visitor row taps and options button taps to the same unknown-device action flow.
- Routed unknown visitor notification taps to either known-device navigation or the unknown-device action sheet.
- Replaced the compact action dialog with a larger sheet.
- Added known unknown-device details to the sheet: device ID, cached info/slogan, cached location, and visit time.
- Clarified localized explanatory copy across all app locales, including that the position was not shared yet, that adding controls future access, and that ignored devices receive no position data.
- Added unit tests for URI compatibility, scanner prefix compatibility, known-device matching, deep-link routing, and notification routing.
- Updated test matrix, test catalog, and changelog.

Validation performed:

- `./miataru/scripts/test-unit.sh -only-testing:miataruTests/DeviceLinkResolverTests -only-testing:miataruTests/UnknownVisitorAlertLocalizationTests -only-testing:miataruTests/UnknownVisitorAlertEvaluatorTests`
- Result: 19 tests in 3 suites passed.
